page: Hetzner Cloud cpx31 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 4 shared vCPUs and 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, managed via the QEMU hypervisor. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is moderate, averaging 387.44 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 60.53 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though the PassMark memory score is relatively weak. Storage-reliant operations, such as Redis SET and static web serving throughput, also perform in the lower 25% tier.

Given its shared CPU architecture and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the cpx31 offers a budget-friendly hardware profile for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU threads. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, development environments, basic database operations, and moderate computational tasks like small-scale LLM inference, where its average text generation speeds can be leveraged without the premium cost of dedicated resources.

It is best suited for development environments, lightweight web applications, and moderate utility computing.
